words.definition: a person who follows someone on social media
words.example: Her channel has fifty thousand followers.
words.exampleUz: Uning kanalida ellik ming obunachi bor.

words.definition: to put a message or picture online
words.example: He posts a new video every Friday.
words.exampleUz: U har juma yangi video joylaydi.

words.definition: a general direction of change, or something popular for a time
words.example: Short videos are the biggest trend now.
words.exampleUz: Qisqa videolar — hozirgi eng katta trend.

description: Ekologik harakat va shaxsiy odatlar haqida gapirish.
story: Do'stingiz plastikdan voz kechdi. Ba'zi fe'llarda -ing va to + fe'l ma'noni o'zgartiradi: stop buying — sotib olishni to'xtatish, stop to think — o'ylash uchun to'xtash.
grammarFocus: stop doing / stop to do, remember doing / remember to do

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: I've stopped buying disposable cups. I carry my own now.
dialogue.uz: Bir martalik stakan sotib olishni to'xtatdim. Endi o'zimnikini olib yuraman.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Good for you! Why did you start?
dialogue.uz: Barakalla! Nega boshladingiz?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: I met an activist at university. I remember signing her petition.
dialogue.uz: Universitetda bir faol bilan tanishdim. Uning petitsiyasiga imzo chekkanim esimda.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: What was the campaign about?
dialogue.uz: Kampaniya nima haqida edi?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: A ban on plastic bags in our city. Most of them end up in landfill.
dialogue.uz: Shahrimizda plastik paketlarni taqiqlash haqida. Ularning ko'pchiligi axlatxonaga tushadi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Did it work?
dialogue.uz: Natija berdimi?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Partly. There was a big protest, and public awareness grew a lot.
dialogue.uz: Qisman. Katta norozilik namoyishi bo'ldi va jamoatchilik xabardorligi ancha oshdi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I should stop to think before I buy things with so much packaging.
dialogue.uz: Men ham ko'p qadoqli narsalarni sotib olishdan oldin to'xtab o'ylashim kerak.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Exactly. A sustainable life starts with small choices. Remember to bring your own bag!
dialogue.uz: Aynan. Barqaror hayot kichik tanlovlardan boshlanadi. O'z sumkangizni olib kelishni unutmang!

words.definition: made to be used once and then thrown away
words.example: Many cafés no longer use disposable cups.
words.exampleUz: Ko'p kafelar endi bir martalik stakan ishlatmaydi.

words.definition: a person who works to bring social or political change
words.example: She is a well-known climate activist.

words.definition: a document signed by many people asking for change
words.example: Over ten thousand people signed the petition.
words.exampleUz: Petitsiyaga o'n mingdan ortiq kishi imzo chekdi.

words.definition: a planned series of actions to achieve a goal
words.example: The campaign encourages people to plant trees.

words.definition: an official rule that stops something
words.example: There is a ban on smoking in restaurants.

words.definition: a place where rubbish is buried in the ground
words.example: Most plastic ends up in landfill.
words.exampleUz: Plastikning ko'p qismi axlat poligoniga tushadi.

words.definition: a public event where people show they disagree
words.example: Students held a protest outside the ministry.
words.exampleUz: Talabalar vazirlik oldida norozilik namoyishi o'tkazishdi.

words.definition: knowledge or understanding of a problem
words.example: The film raised awareness of water pollution.
words.exampleUz: Film suv ifloslanishi haqida xabardorlikni oshirdi.

words.definition: the material used to wrap goods
words.example: Too much packaging is bad for nature.

words.definition: able to continue without harming the environment
words.example: We need more sustainable ways to travel.
words.exampleUz: Bizga sayohat qilishning barqarorroq usullari kerak.

description: Yutuqlar va joriy ishlar haqida aniq gapirish.
story: Siz yuqori lavozimga suhbatdasiz. Tugallangan natija uchun Present Perfect Simple (I've recruited four people), hali davom etayotgan ish uchun Present Perfect Continuous (I've been leading a project) ishlatiladi.
grammarFocus: Present Perfect Simple / Continuous: I've implemented… / I've been leading…

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.en: What have you accomplished in your current role?
dialogue.uz: Hozirgi lavozimingizda nimalarga erishdingiz?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I've implemented a new online system, and I've recruited four new people.
dialogue.uz: Yangi onlayn tizimni joriy qildim va to'rtta yangi xodim yolladim.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.en: And what have you been working on recently?
dialogue.uz: So'nggi paytda nima ustida ishlayapsiz?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I've been leading a project to improve our company's reputation online.
dialogue.uz: Kompaniyamizning internetdagi obro'sini oshirish loyihasiga rahbarlik qilyapman.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.en: How do you handle pressure?
dialogue.uz: Bosimni qanday yengasiz?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I stay calm and plan carefully. I've always worked well under pressure.
dialogue.uz: Xotirjam turaman va puxta reja tuzaman. Bosim ostida doim yaxshi ishlaganman.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.en: Can you give an example of initiative?
dialogue.uz: Tashabbus ko'rsatganingizga misol keltira olasizmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Last year I started English lessons for my colleagues. I'm very motivated to share what I know.
dialogue.uz: O'tgan yili hamkasblarim uchun ingliz tili darslarini boshladim. Bilganlarimni ulashishga juda ishtiyoqmandman.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.en: How would your expertise contribute to our team?
dialogue.uz: Sizning tajribangiz jamoamizga qanday hissa qo'shadi?

words.definition: to succeed in doing something
words.example: We accomplished a lot this year.

words.definition: to start using a plan or system
words.example: The school implemented a new timetable.
words.exampleUz: Maktab yangi dars jadvalini joriy qildi.

words.definition: to find new people to work for a company
words.example: The company plans to recruit fifty engineers.

words.definition: what people think about someone or something
words.example: The hotel has an excellent reputation.

words.definition: to deal with a difficult situation
words.example: She handled the angry customer very well.
words.exampleUz: U jahli chiqqan mijozni juda yaxshi uddaladi.

words.definition: the feeling that you must do a lot or do it quickly
words.example: Students feel a lot of pressure before exams.
words.exampleUz: Talabalar imtihon oldidan katta bosimni his qiladi.

words.definition: the ability to decide and act without being told
words.example: He showed initiative and solved the problem himself.
words.exampleUz: U tashabbus ko'rsatib, muammoni o'zi hal qildi.

words.definition: wanting to do something and work hard at it
words.example: We are looking for motivated students.

words.definition: special skill or knowledge
words.example: We need someone with expertise in finance.
words.exampleUz: Bizga moliya bo'yicha tajribali odam kerak.

words.definition: to give something to help achieve a result
words.example: Everyone contributed ideas to the project.
words.exampleUz: Hamma loyihaga o'z g'oyalari bilan hissa qo'shdi.

description: Yangi mamlakatga moslashish tajribasi haqida gapirish.
story: Do'stingiz Germaniyaga ko'chib ketgan. Yangi narsaga o'rganish jarayoni get used to (o'rganib qolmoq), o'rganib bo'lingan holat esa be used to (o'rgangan) bilan ifodalanadi. Ikkalasidan keyin -ing keladi.
grammarFocus: be used to / get used to + -ing

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: How's life in Germany? Have you got used to it?
dialogue.uz: Germaniyada hayot qanday? O'rganib qoldingizmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Slowly. At first everything was unfamiliar — the language, the culture, even the food.
dialogue.uz: Asta-sekin. Avvaliga hamma narsa notanish edi — til, madaniyat, hatto ovqat ham.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Do you miss Uzbek cuisine?
dialogue.uz: O'zbek taomlarini sog'inasizmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Terribly! I'm still not used to eating dinner at six. And I often feel homesick.
dialogue.uz: Juda! Kechki ovqatni soat oltida yeyishga hali o'rganmadim. Tez-tez vatanimni sog'inaman.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Was it hard to get a visa?
dialogue.uz: Viza olish qiyin bo'ldimi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: The bureaucracy was terrible. My residence permit took four months.
dialogue.uz: Byurokratiya dahshatli edi. Yashash ruxsatnomam to'rt oy vaqt oldi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Are there many immigrants in your city?
dialogue.uz: Shahringizda muhojirlar ko'pmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Yes, and most of them integrate well. You just need time to adapt.
dialogue.uz: Ha, ularning ko'pchiligi jamiyatga yaxshi moslashadi. Faqat ko'nikish uchun vaqt kerak.

words.definition: not known to you
words.example: The city was unfamiliar to me.

words.definition: the customs, art and beliefs of a group of people
words.example: I am interested in Japanese culture.

words.definition: a style of cooking of a country
words.example: Uzbek cuisine is famous for plov.

words.definition: sad because you are far from home
words.example: Students often feel homesick in their first year.
words.exampleUz: Talabalar birinchi yilda ko'pincha uyini sog'inadi.

words.definition: an official document that allows you to enter a country
words.example: You need a visa to visit the UK.
words.exampleUz: Buyuk Britaniyaga borish uchun viza kerak.

words.definition: complicated official rules and processes
words.example: There is too much bureaucracy in this office.

words.definition: the place where you live officially
words.example: He got a residence permit for two years.
words.exampleUz: U ikki yillik yashash ruxsatnomasini oldi.

words.definition: a person who comes to live in another country
words.example: Many immigrants work in construction.

words.definition: to become part of a group or society
words.example: Learning the language helps you integrate.
words.exampleUz: Tilni o'rganish jamiyatga moslashishga yordam beradi.

words.definition: to change your behaviour to suit a new situation
words.example: Children adapt quickly to new schools.

description: Rasmiy bahsda fikr bildirish va e'tiroz qilish.
story: Siz ta'lim haqidagi teledebatdasiz. "I think" o'rniga rasmiyroq iboralar ishlatiladi: From my perspective, I'd argue that, It seems to me that, In my view.
grammarFocus: Rasmiy fikr: From my perspective… / I'd argue that… / It seems to me that…

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.en: Today's debate: should schools focus less on exams?
dialogue.uz: Bugungi bahs: maktablar imtihonlarga kamroq e'tibor berishi kerakmi?

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: From my perspective, yes. Students memorise facts and forget them the next day.
dialogue.uz: Mening nuqtai nazarimdan, ha. O'quvchilar faktlarni yodlab, ertasi kuni unutishadi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I'd argue that exams are still necessary. We need some form of assessment.
dialogue.uz: Menimcha, imtihonlar baribir zarur. Bizga qandaydir baholash shakli kerak.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: Of course, but the curriculum should develop critical thinking and creativity.
dialogue.uz: Albatta, lekin o'quv dasturi tanqidiy fikrlash va ijodkorlikni rivojlantirishi kerak.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: It seems to me that teachers can't evaluate creativity fairly.
dialogue.uz: Menimcha, o'qituvchilar ijodkorlikni adolatli baholay olmaydi.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.en: What about university? Should tuition be free?
dialogue.uz: Universitet-chi? O'qish bepul bo'lishi kerakmi?

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: In my view, school is compulsory, so university should at least be affordable.
dialogue.uz: Mening fikrimcha, maktab majburiy, shuning uchun universitet hech bo'lmaganda hamyonbop bo'lishi kerak.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I partly agree, but free tuition must be paid for by taxes.
dialogue.uz: Qisman qo'shilaman, lekin bepul ta'lim soliqlar hisobidan to'lanishi kerak.

words.definition: a formal discussion where people express different opinions
words.example: The debate lasted two hours.

words.definition: a particular way of thinking about something
words.example: Try to see it from my perspective.
words.exampleUz: Bunga mening nuqtai nazarimdan qarashga harakat qiling.

words.definition: to learn something so that you remember it exactly
words.example: I memorised the poem in one evening.

words.definition: the process of judging how good someone’s work is
words.example: The final assessment is a written test.

words.definition: the subjects taught in a school or course
words.example: Computer science is now part of the curriculum.

words.definition: judging something carefully, considering good and bad points
words.example: Critical thinking is an important skill.

words.definition: the ability to make new and original things
words.example: Art classes develop creativity.

words.definition: to judge how good or important something is
words.example: We need to evaluate the results carefully.

words.definition: the money you pay for teaching, especially at university
words.example: Tuition fees have gone up again.

words.definition: that must be done because of a rule
words.example: English is a compulsory subject.

description: Iste'mol odatlari haqida urg'u bilan gapirish.
story: Do'stingiz arzon "tez moda"dan voz kechgan. Gapning bir qismiga urg'u berish uchun What I love is… yoki It was … that… tuzilmasi ishlatiladi — o'zbek tilidagi "…gan narsa — …" ga o'xshaydi.
grammarFocus: Urg'uli gap (cleft): What I love is… / It was a film that…

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: What I love about your style is that it's unique. Where do you shop?
dialogue.uz: Uslubingizda menga yoqadigani — u noyob. Qayerdan xarid qilasiz?

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: Mostly vintage shops. What I don't want is another cheap T-shirt from a big brand.
dialogue.uz: Asosan vintaj do'konlardan. Men xohlamaydigan narsa — katta brendning navbatdagi arzon futbolkasi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Why not? Fast fashion is so cheap.
dialogue.uz: Nega? Tez moda juda arzon-ku.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: It was a documentary that changed my mind. It showed the impact of cheap clothes on nature.
dialogue.uz: Fikrimni o'zgartirgan narsa bitta hujjatli film bo'ldi. Unda arzon kiyimlarning tabiatga ta'siri ko'rsatilgan.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: And the workers?
dialogue.uz: Ishchilar-chi?

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: Many of them earn a terrible wage. So now I always read the label.
dialogue.uz: Ularning ko'pchiligi juda kam maosh oladi. Shuning uchun endi doim yorliqni o'qiyman.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: What do you look for?
dialogue.uz: Nimaga qaraysiz?

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: Natural fabric and durable quality. What matters is how long a garment lasts.
dialogue.uz: Tabiiy mato va chidamli sifatga. Muhimi — kiyim qancha vaqtga chidashi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: My wardrobe is full of things I never wear!
dialogue.uz: Mening shkafim hech kiymaydigan narsalarga to'la!

words.definition: old but of high quality
words.example: She collects vintage furniture.

words.definition: a name given to a product by the company that makes it
words.example: Which brand of phone do you have?

words.definition: the style of clothes that is popular at a time
words.example: She works in the fashion industry.

words.definition: a strong effect that something has
words.example: Tourism has a big impact on the economy.

words.definition: money paid for work, usually every week
words.example: The minimum wage has increased.

words.definition: a piece of paper or cloth with information about a product
words.example: Read the label before you wash it.

words.definition: cloth used for making clothes
words.example: Cotton is a natural fabric.

words.definition: lasting for a long time
words.example: These boots are very durable.

words.definition: a piece of clothing
words.example: Each garment is made by hand.

words.definition: a tall cupboard for clothes; also all the clothes you own
words.example: My wardrobe is too small for my clothes.

description: O'tmishdagi uzoq jarayonni hikoya qilish.
story: Penitsillin qanday kashf etilgani haqidagi hikoya. O'tmishdagi voqeadan OLDIN uzoq davom etgan jarayon uchun Past Perfect Continuous ishlatiladi: He had been studying… before…
grammarFocus: Past Perfect Continuous: He had been studying bacteria for years

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Do you know how penicillin was discovered?
dialogue.uz: Penitsillin qanday kashf etilganini bilasizmi?

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.en: Wasn't it an accident?
dialogue.uz: Tasodif emasmidi?

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Partly. Alexander Fleming had been studying bacteria in his laboratory for years.
dialogue.uz: Qisman. Aleksandr Fleming yillar davomida laboratoriyasida bakteriyalarni o'rganib kelgan edi.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.en: What happened?
dialogue.uz: Nima bo'ldi?

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: He had been working on an experiment before his holiday, and he accidentally left some dishes open.
dialogue.uz: U ta'tildan oldin bir tajriba ustida ishlagan va tasodifan bir nechta idishni ochiq qoldirgan.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.en: And when he came back?
dialogue.uz: Qaytib kelganida-chi?

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: He observed that a mould had killed the bacteria. He checked it under a microscope.
dialogue.uz: U mog'or bakteriyalarni o'ldirganini kuzatdi. Buni mikroskop ostida tekshirdi.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.en: So a mistake became a breakthrough!
dialogue.uz: Demak, xato kashfiyotga aylandi!

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Yes. But the discovery only mattered because of his research. Other scientists had been testing his theory for ten years before the medicine was ready.
dialogue.uz: Ha. Lekin kashfiyot faqat uning tadqiqotlari tufayli ahamiyat kasb etdi. Boshqa olimlar dori tayyor bo'lgunicha o'n yil davomida uning nazariyasini sinab kelgan edi.

words.definition: very small living things, some of which cause disease
words.example: Wash your hands to remove bacteria.
words.exampleUz: Bakteriyalardan xalos bo'lish uchun qo'lingizni yuving.

words.definition: a room where scientists do experiments
words.example: The samples were sent to a laboratory.

words.definition: a scientific test to learn something
words.example: We did an experiment with water and salt.
words.exampleUz: Suv va tuz bilan tajriba o'tkazdik.

words.definition: by chance, without planning
words.example: I accidentally deleted the file.

words.definition: to watch something carefully
words.example: Scientists observed the birds for a year.
words.exampleUz: Olimlar qushlarni bir yil davomida kuzatishdi.

words.definition: a tool that makes very small things look bigger
words.example: Look at the cells under the microscope.

words.definition: an important new discovery
words.example: The new drug is a medical breakthrough.

words.definition: the act of finding something new
words.example: The discovery of oil changed the region.
words.exampleUz: Neft kashf etilishi mintaqani o'zgartirib yubordi.

words.definition: careful study to discover new facts
words.example: She is doing research on climate change.
words.exampleUz: U iqlim o'zgarishi bo'yicha tadqiqot olib bormoqda.

words.definition: an idea that tries to explain something
words.example: Einstein’s theory changed physics.

description: Nizoni tasvirlash va yechim taklif qilish.
story: Ofisda ikki hamkasb urishib qoldi. Kundalik nutqda bitta fe'l o'rniga ko'pincha frazali fe'l ishlatiladi: fall out (urishib qolmoq), get along (til topishmoq), bring up (masalani ko'tarmoq), sort out (hal qilmoq).
grammarFocus: Frazali fe'llar: fall out, get along, bring up, point out, sort out

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: There's a lot of tension in the office. What's going on?
dialogue.uz: Ofisda keskinlik ko'p. Nima bo'lyapti?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Rustam and Dilnoza have fallen out. They can't get along any more.
dialogue.uz: Rustam bilan Dilnoza urishib qolishdi. Endi til topisha olishmayapti.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Why? What started the conflict?
dialogue.uz: Nega? Nizoni nima boshladi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: In the meeting, Rustam kept interrupting her, and then he criticised her report in front of everyone.
dialogue.uz: Yig'ilishda Rustam uning gapini bo'lib turdi, keyin hammaning oldida hisobotini tanqid qildi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: That's not respectful. Did she complain?
dialogue.uz: Bu hurmatsizlik. U shikoyat qildimi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: She's frustrated, but she doesn't want to bring it up with the boss.
dialogue.uz: Uning jahli chiqqan, lekin bu masalani rahbarga ko'tarishni istamaydi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Someone should point out that feedback must be constructive, not personal.
dialogue.uz: Kimdir fikr-mulohaza shaxsiy emas, balki foydali bo'lishi kerakligini ta'kidlashi kerak.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Exactly. And his tone was aggressive. He blames others for everything.
dialogue.uz: Aynan. Uning ohangi ham tajovuzkor edi. U hamma narsada boshqalarni ayblaydi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Let's help them sort it out before it gets worse.
dialogue.uz: Keling, vaziyat yomonlashmasdan ularga masalani hal qilishga yordam beraylik.

words.definition: a feeling of worry or anger between people
words.example: You could feel the tension in the room.

words.definition: a serious disagreement
words.example: The manager helped to sort out the conflict.
words.exampleUz: Menejer nizoni hal qilishga yordam berdi.

words.definition: to stop someone while they are speaking
words.example: Please do not interrupt me.

words.definition: to say what you think is bad about someone or something
words.example: The film was criticised for being too long.
words.exampleUz: Film juda uzunligi uchun tanqid qilindi.

words.definition: showing respect for other people
words.example: Be respectful even when you disagree.

words.definition: annoyed because you cannot do what you want
words.example: I get frustrated when my computer is slow.

words.definition: comments about how well someone has done something
words.example: Thank you for your helpful feedback.

words.definition: helpful and intended to improve something
words.example: Constructive criticism helps people grow.
words.exampleUz: Foydali tanqid odamlarning o'sishiga yordam beradi.

words.definition: the quality of a voice that shows feelings
words.example: I did not like the tone of his email.

words.definition: to say that someone is responsible for something bad
words.example: Do not blame yourself for the mistake.

description: Xato qarorlar va huquqlar haqida gapirish.
story: Siz nosoz buyum sotib oldingiz va do'kon pulni qaytarishni istamayapti. O'tmishdagi xatoni baholashda should have done (qilish kerak edi) va shouldn't have done (qilmaslik kerak edi) ishlatiladi.
grammarFocus: O'tmishdagi tanqid: should have / shouldn't have + V3

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: The shop overcharged me for this washing machine. And now it doesn't work.
dialogue.uz: Do'kon bu kir yuvish mashinasi uchun mendan ortiqcha pul oldi. Endi esa u ishlamayapti.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: You should have checked the price on the receipt.
dialogue.uz: Chekdagi narxni tekshirishingiz kerak edi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I know. I shouldn't have trusted the salesman. The advert was designed to mislead customers.
dialogue.uz: Bilaman. Sotuvchiga ishonmasligim kerak edi. Reklama mijozlarni chalg'itish uchun tuzilgan ekan.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: As a consumer, you're entitled to a refund or a repair.
dialogue.uz: Iste'molchi sifatida siz pulni qaytarib olish yoki ta'mirlatish huquqiga egasiz.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Really? The shop says it's against their policy.
dialogue.uz: Rostdanmi? Do'kon bu ularning qoidalariga zid deydi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Their policy can't be above the law. You have legal rights.
dialogue.uz: Ularning qoidalari qonundan ustun bo'la olmaydi. Sizning qonuniy huquqlaringiz bor.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: So what should I do?
dialogue.uz: Unda nima qilishim kerak?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Write a formal complaint and keep proof of your purchase. You can also claim compensation for the extra money.
dialogue.uz: Rasmiy shikoyat yozing va xarid dalilini saqlang. Ortiqcha pul uchun kompensatsiya ham talab qilishingiz mumkin.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I should have done that from the start.
dialogue.uz: Buni boshidanoq qilishim kerak ekan.

words.definition: to ask someone to pay too much
words.example: The taxi driver tried to overcharge us.
words.exampleUz: Taksi haydovchisi bizdan ortiqcha pul olmoqchi bo'ldi.

words.definition: to make someone believe something that is not true
words.example: The advert may mislead young people.

words.definition: a person who buys goods or services
words.example: Consumers want cheaper prices.

words.definition: having the right to have or do something
words.example: You are entitled to twenty days of holiday.

words.definition: a set of rules that an organisation follows
words.example: The shop has a strict returns policy.

words.definition: connected with the law or allowed by law
words.example: Is it legal to park here?

words.definition: a statement that something is wrong or not good enough
words.example: We received many complaints about the noise.

words.definition: something that you buy
words.example: Keep the receipt as proof of purchase.

words.definition: to ask for something because you have a right to it
words.example: You can claim your money back.

words.definition: money paid to someone because of loss or damage
words.example: The airline paid compensation for the delay.

description: Keng tarqalgan fikrlarni tanqidiy tekshirish.
story: Buvingizning ba'zi maslahatlari haqiqatmi yoki afsona? Kim aytgani noma'lum yoki muhim bo'lmagan fikrlarni yetkazishda It is believed that… va is said to be… tuzilmalari ishlatiladi.
grammarFocus: Shaxssiz majhul: It is believed that… / It is said to be…

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: It is believed that you shouldn't drink cold water after plov. Is that true?
dialogue.uz: Palovdan keyin sovuq suv ichmaslik kerak, degan ishonch bor. Bu rostmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: It's a popular belief, but there's no scientific evidence for it.
dialogue.uz: Bu keng tarqalgan ishonch, lekin buning ilmiy isboti yo'q.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: My grandmother says it makes food harder to digest.
dialogue.uz: Buvim bu ovqatni hazm qilishni qiyinlashtiradi deydi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: It is said to be bad, but nobody has managed to prove it. It's a myth.
dialogue.uz: Zararli deyishadi, lekin hech kim buni isbotlay olmagan. Bu afsona.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: What about vitamin supplements? Are they really good for the immune system?
dialogue.uz: Vitamin qo'shimchalari-chi? Ular rostdan ham immunitet uchun foydalimi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Only if your nutrition is poor. A normal diet usually gives you enough.
dialogue.uz: Faqat ovqatlanishingiz yomon bo'lsa. Oddiy ratsion odatda yetarlicha beradi.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: And coffee? Some people say it's harmful.
dialogue.uz: Qahva-chi? Ba'zilar u zararli deydi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: In moderate amounts, it's fine. Just drink enough water and stay hydrated.
dialogue.uz: Me'yorida ichilsa, zarari yo'q. Faqat yetarlicha suv iching va tanangizni suvsiz qoldirmang.

words.definition: an idea that you accept as true
words.example: It is a common belief that carrots help your eyes.
words.exampleUz: Sabzi ko'z uchun foydali degan keng tarqalgan ishonch bor.

words.definition: connected with science
words.example: There is no scientific proof for this.

words.definition: to change food in your stomach so the body can use it
words.example: Fatty food is hard to digest.

words.definition: to show that something is true
words.example: Can you prove that he was there?
words.exampleUz: Uning u yerda bo'lganini isbotlay olasizmi?

words.definition: an idea that many people believe but that is not true
words.example: It is a myth that we only use ten percent of our brain.
words.exampleUz: Miyamizning faqat o'n foizini ishlatamiz, degan gap — afsona.

words.definition: a pill that adds vitamins or minerals to your diet
words.example: Many people take vitamin D supplements in winter.
words.exampleUz: Ko'p odamlar qishda D vitamini qo'shimchasini ichadi.

words.definition: connected with the body’s protection from disease
words.example: Sleep helps your immune system.

words.definition: the food that you eat and how it affects your health
words.example: Good nutrition is important for children.

words.definition: neither too much nor too little
words.example: Moderate exercise is good for everyone.
words.exampleUz: Me'yoriy jismoniy mashq hamma uchun foydali.

words.definition: having enough water in your body
words.example: Drink water to stay hydrated in summer.

description: Ideal rahbar sifatlarini tasvirlash.
story: Siz ishlagan eng yaxshi rahbar haqida gapiryapsiz. Egalikni ko'rsatish uchun whose (kimning), rasmiy nutqda predlog bilan esa whom ishlatiladi: the people to whom he gave tasks.
grammarFocus: whose / whom / from whom

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Who is the best leader you have ever worked with?
dialogue.uz: Siz ishlagan eng yaxshi rahbar kim?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: My first boss, whose vision changed our small company.
dialogue.uz: Birinchi rahbarim — uning uzoqni ko'ra bilishi kichik kompaniyamizni o'zgartirib yubordi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: What made him special?
dialogue.uz: Uni nima alohida qilgan?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: He was decisive but humble. He never used his authority to scare people.
dialogue.uz: U qat'iyatli, lekin kamtar edi. Hech qachon odamlarni qo'rqitish uchun hokimiyatidan foydalanmagan.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Did he manage everything himself?
dialogue.uz: Hamma narsani o'zi boshqarganmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: No. He knew how to delegate, and he trusted the people to whom he gave tasks.
dialogue.uz: Yo'q. U vakolat berishni bilardi va vazifa bergan odamlariga ishonardi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: It sounds like he really inspired you.
dialogue.uz: U sizni haqiqatan ilhomlantirgan ekan.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: He did. He was my mentor — the person from whom I learned empathy.
dialogue.uz: Ha. U mening ustozim edi — men undan hamdardlikni o'rgandim.

words.definition: a person who leads a group or organisation
words.example: A good leader listens to the team.

words.definition: a clear idea of what the future should be
words.example: The founder had a vision of a green city.
words.exampleUz: Asoschining yashil shahar haqida aniq g'oyasi bor edi.

words.definition: able to make decisions quickly
words.example: We need a decisive manager.

words.definition: not thinking you are better than other people
words.example: Despite his success, he stayed humble.
words.exampleUz: Muvaffaqiyatiga qaramay, u kamtar bo'lib qoldi.

words.definition: the power to give orders
words.example: Teachers have authority in the classroom.

words.definition: to control or organise a business or team
words.example: She manages a team of twelve people.
words.exampleUz: U o'n ikki kishilik jamoani boshqaradi.

words.definition: to give part of your work to someone else
words.example: Good managers delegate tasks.

words.definition: to give someone the wish to do something
words.example: Her story inspired many young people.

words.definition: an experienced person who advises someone younger
words.example: Every new teacher has a mentor.
words.exampleUz: Har bir yangi o'qituvchining ustozi bor.

words.definition: the ability to understand other people’s feelings
words.example: Nurses need a lot of empathy.

description: Voqealar ketma-ketligini jonli hikoya qilish.
story: Sayohatingizda hamma narsa noto'g'ri ketdi. Yaxshi hikoyada zamonlar birga ishlaydi: fon uchun Past Continuous (while I was buying), asosiy voqealar uchun Past Simple, undan oldingi voqea uchun Past Perfect (I had left it).
grammarFocus: Hikoya zamonlari: Past Simple, Past Continuous, Past Perfect birga

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: How was your trip to Istanbul?
dialogue.uz: Istanbulga safaringiz qanday o'tdi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: A real adventure! On the first day, while I was buying souvenirs, a pickpocket took my wallet.
dialogue.uz: Haqiqiy sarguzasht! Birinchi kuni esdalik sovg'alar sotib olayotganimda cho'ntakkesar hamyonimni olib qo'ydi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Oh no! Was your passport in it?
dialogue.uz: Voy! Pasportingiz ham ichidamidi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: No, luckily I had left it in my backpack. But I still had to go to the embassy for a document.
dialogue.uz: Yo'q, xayriyatki, uni ryukzagimda qoldirgandim. Lekin baribir bir hujjat uchun elchixonaga borishimga to'g'ri keldi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: And the hotel?
dialogue.uz: Mehmonxona-chi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: When I arrived, the girl at reception said the hotel was overbooked!
dialogue.uz: Kelganimda qabulxonadagi qiz mehmonxonada joy qolmaganini aytdi!

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: So where did you stay?
dialogue.uz: Unda qayerda qoldingiz?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: In a cheap hostel. Then my flight home was delayed, and I was stranded at the airport for a night.
dialogue.uz: Arzon hostelda. Keyin uyga reysim kechikdi va bir kecha aeroportda qolib ketdim.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Your itinerary didn't go as planned at all!
dialogue.uz: Rejangiz umuman o'ylaganingizdek ketmabdi!

words.definition: an exciting and unusual experience
words.example: Our trip to the mountains was a real adventure.

words.definition: something you buy to remember a place
words.example: I bought a small plate as a souvenir.
words.exampleUz: Esdalik uchun kichik likopcha sotib oldim.

words.definition: a thief who steals from people’s pockets
words.example: Be careful of pickpockets on the metro.

words.definition: a bag that you carry on your back
words.example: He travelled around Asia with just a backpack.
words.exampleUz: U Osiyo bo'ylab faqat ryukzak bilan sayohat qildi.

words.definition: the official office of a country in a foreign capital
words.example: You can get a new passport at the embassy.

words.definition: the place in a hotel where guests go when they arrive
words.example: Please leave your key at reception.

words.definition: having sold more places than are available
words.example: The flight was overbooked, so I took the next one.
words.exampleUz: Reysda joy qolmagani uchun keyingisiga chiqdim.

words.definition: a cheap place to stay, often with shared rooms
words.example: Students often stay in hostels.

words.definition: unable to leave a place
words.example: Hundreds of passengers were stranded by the snow.
words.exampleUz: Qor sababli yuzlab yo'lovchilar qolib ketdi.

words.definition: a plan of a journey
words.example: Send me your itinerary before you leave.

description: Onlayn firibgarlikni tanish va undan himoyalanish.
story: Sizga "bankdan" shubhali xabar keldi. Qoida yoki kutilgan xatti-harakatni ifodalash uchun be supposed to ishlatiladi: What am I supposed to do? — Nima qilishim kerak?
grammarFocus: be supposed to: Banks aren't supposed to ask for…

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: I got a message from 'my bank' asking me to click a link and verify my card.
dialogue.uz: 'Bankim'dan kartamni tasdiqlash uchun havolani bosishimni so'ragan xabar oldim.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Don't click it! It's a scam. Banks aren't supposed to ask for your details by SMS.
dialogue.uz: Bosmang! Bu firibgarlik. Banklar ma'lumotlaringizni SMS orqali so'ramasligi kerak.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: It looked real, though.
dialogue.uz: Lekin haqiqiyga o'xshardi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: That's how fraud works. They wanted to steal your identity.
dialogue.uz: Firibgarlik shunday ishlaydi. Ular shaxsingizga oid ma'lumotlarni o'g'irlamoqchi edi.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: What am I supposed to do now?
dialogue.uz: Endi nima qilishim kerak?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Call the bank and report it. And never open an attachment from a suspicious email.
dialogue.uz: Bankka qo'ng'iroq qilib, xabar bering. Shubhali xatdagi ilova faylni hech qachon ochmang.

dialogue.speaker: Malika
dialogue.en: Should I install antivirus software?
dialogue.uz: Antivirus dasturini o'rnatishim kerakmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Yes, and use an app that can encrypt your messages. Also make a backup of your photos every month.
dialogue.uz: Ha, xabarlaringizni shifrlaydigan ilovadan foydalaning. Har oy suratlaringizning zaxira nusxasini ham oling.

words.definition: a connection to another page on the internet
words.example: Click the link to open the file.

words.definition: to check that something is true or correct
words.example: Please verify your email address.

words.definition: a dishonest plan to get money
words.example: That job offer was a scam.

words.definition: the crime of cheating people to get money
words.example: Card fraud is increasing.

words.definition: who someone is, or the details that prove it
words.example: Criminals can steal your identity online.
words.exampleUz: Jinoyatchilar internetda shaxsiy ma'lumotlaringizni o'g'irlashi mumkin.

words.definition: a file sent with an email
words.example: I have sent the report as an attachment.

words.definition: making you think something is wrong
words.example: Report any suspicious messages.
words.exampleUz: Har qanday shubhali xabar haqida xabar bering.

words.definition: designed to protect a computer from viruses
words.example: Keep your antivirus program updated.

words.definition: to change information into a secret code
words.example: The app encrypts all messages.

words.definition: a copy of data that you keep in case the original is lost
words.example: Always make a backup of important files.
words.exampleUz: Muhim fayllarning doim zaxira nusxasini oling.

description: Filmga batafsil baho berish.
story: Yangi film haqida tanqidiy fikr bildiryapsiz. -ing sifatlar narsa qanday ekanini (confusing — chalkash), -ed sifatlar esa odam nimani his qilganini (confused — chalkashib qolgan) bildiradi.
grammarFocus: -ed / -ing sifatlar: amazed / amazing, confused / confusing

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Did you read what the critic wrote about the new Uzbek film?
dialogue.uz: Tanqidchi yangi o'zbek filmi haqida nima yozganini o'qidingizmi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Yes, but I disagree. He says it's overrated.
dialogue.uz: Ha, lekin qo'shilmayman. U filmni ortiqcha maqtalgan deydi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: I found the story a bit predictable.
dialogue.uz: Menimcha, voqealar biroz oldindan bilinib qoladi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Really? The twist at the end was gripping! I was amazed.
dialogue.uz: Rostdanmi? Oxiridagi kutilmagan burilish hayajonli edi! Men hayratda qoldim.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: The middle part was confusing, though. I was bored for twenty minutes.
dialogue.uz: Lekin o'rta qismi chalkash edi. Yigirma daqiqa zerikdim.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Maybe. But the cast was brilliant, especially the old man.
dialogue.uz: Balki. Lekin aktyorlar tarkibi zo'r edi, ayniqsa chol.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: I agree. And the soundtrack was beautiful.
dialogue.uz: Qo'shilaman. Musiqasi ham chiroyli edi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: So it wasn't disappointing after all?
dialogue.uz: Demak, umuman umidsizlantirmadimi?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Not at all. I'd give it four stars out of five.
dialogue.uz: Aslo. Beshdan to'rt yulduz qo'yardim.

words.definition: a person whose job is to give opinions about films, books or art
words.example: The critic loved the new play.

words.definition: thought to be better than it really is
words.example: In my opinion, that restaurant is overrated.

words.definition: happening in a way you expected
words.example: The ending was too predictable.
words.exampleUz: Yakuni juda oldindan bilinib qolgan edi.

words.definition: an unexpected change in a story
words.example: The book has a clever twist at the end.
words.exampleUz: Kitob oxirida ajoyib kutilmagan burilish bor.

words.definition: so exciting that you cannot stop watching or reading
words.example: It was a gripping story from start to finish.
words.exampleUz: Bu boshidan oxirigacha hayajonli hikoya edi.

words.definition: very surprised
words.example: I was amazed by how fast she learned.
words.exampleUz: Uning qanchalik tez o'rganganidan hayratda qoldim.

words.definition: difficult to understand
words.example: The instructions were confusing.

words.definition: all the actors in a film or play
words.example: The film has a famous cast.

words.definition: the music of a film
words.example: I listen to the soundtrack every day.

words.definition: not as good as you hoped
words.example: The results were disappointing.

description: Omma oldida gapirishga tayyorlanish.
story: Singlingizning to'yida nutq so'zlashingiz kerak. Ikki fikrni kuchli bog'lash uchun not only… but also ishlatiladi. Gap boshida kelsa, so'z tartibi savol gapdagidek o'zgaradi: Not only will you remember…
grammarFocus: Not only… but also… / Not only will you…, but you'll also…

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I have to give a speech at my sister's wedding, and I'm really nervous.
dialogue.uz: Singlimning to'yida nutq so'zlashim kerak va juda hayajondaman.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: That's normal. Not only beginners but also famous speakers feel anxiety.
dialogue.uz: Bu tabiiy. Nafaqat yangi boshlovchilar, balki mashhur notiqlar ham xavotirni his qiladi.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: How can I feel more confident?
dialogue.uz: Qanday qilib o'zimga ishonchliroq bo'la olaman?

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Rehearse it at least five times. Not only will you remember it better, but you'll also relax.
dialogue.uz: Uni kamida besh marta mashq qiling. Nafaqat yaxshiroq eslab qolasiz, balki xotirjam ham bo'lasiz.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: What about my hands? I never know what to do with them.
dialogue.uz: Qo'llarim-chi? Ular bilan nima qilishni hech bilmayman.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Use natural gestures. And don't be afraid to pause — silence can be powerful.
dialogue.uz: Tabiiy imo-ishoralardan foydalaning. To'xtab olishdan qo'rqmang — sukunat ta'sirli bo'lishi mumkin.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I want to impress everyone.
dialogue.uz: Hammani hayratda qoldirmoqchiman.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Don't try to impress — try to engage people. Tell a short story. That's how you persuade and touch hearts.
dialogue.uz: Hayratga solishga emas, odamlarni o'zingizga jalb qilishga harakat qiling. Qisqa hikoya aytib bering. Ishontirish va qalblarga yetib borish shunday bo'ladi.

words.definition: a formal talk given to an audience
words.example: The president gave a speech on television.

words.definition: worried and a little afraid
words.example: I always feel nervous before exams.

words.definition: a feeling of worry and fear
words.example: Exercise can reduce anxiety.

words.definition: sure that you can do something well
words.example: She is a confident speaker.

words.definition: to practise a speech or performance before the real event
words.example: The actors rehearse every evening.
words.exampleUz: Aktyorlar har kuni kechqurun mashq qilishadi.

words.definition: a movement of your hands or head to express something
words.example: He made a friendly gesture.

words.definition: to stop speaking for a short time
words.example: She paused before answering the question.
words.exampleUz: U savolga javob berishdan oldin biroz to'xtadi.

words.definition: to make someone admire you
words.example: He tried to impress her with his cooking.
words.exampleUz: U pazandaligi bilan uni hayratda qoldirmoqchi bo'ldi.

words.definition: to attract and keep someone’s interest
words.example: Good teachers engage their students.
words.exampleUz: Yaxshi o'qituvchilar o'quvchilarini o'ziga jalb qiladi.

words.definition: to make someone agree to do or believe something
words.example: I persuaded my father to buy a new car.

description: Kelajak haqida turli darajadagi ishonch bilan gapirish.
story: O'ttiz yildan keyin Toshkent qanday bo'lishini tasavvur qilyapsiz. Ishonch darajasini ko'rsatish uchun bound to (albatta), likely to (ehtimoli katta) va set to (kutilmoqda) ishlatiladi.
grammarFocus: bound to / likely to / set to

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: What will Tashkent look like in thirty years?
dialogue.uz: O'ttiz yildan keyin Toshkent qanday ko'rinishda bo'ladi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: It's bound to be much bigger. The population is likely to reach five million.
dialogue.uz: U albatta ancha katta bo'ladi. Aholisi besh millionga yetishi ehtimoli katta.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: Will there be more skyscrapers?
dialogue.uz: Osmono'par binolar ko'payadimi?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Probably. Higher density means less land is needed as the city expands.
dialogue.uz: Ehtimol. Zichlik yuqoriroq bo'lsa, shahar kengayganda kamroq yer kerak bo'ladi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: And traffic? Congestion is already terrible.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: What do you mean by a smart city?
dialogue.uz: Aqlli shahar deganda nimani nazarda tutasiz?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Traffic lights, water and energy will be controlled by data. And many roofs will have solar panels.
dialogue.uz: Svetoforlar, suv va energiya ma'lumotlar orqali boshqariladi. Ko'p tomlarda quyosh panellari bo'ladi.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.en: That will need a lot of new infrastructure.
dialogue.uz: Buning uchun juda ko'p yangi infratuzilma kerak bo'ladi.

description: Kursni yakunlash va keyingi qadamlarni rejalashtirish.
story: Siz 90-kunga yetdingiz va kursni tugatdingiz! O'qituvchingiz bilan so'nggi suhbat. Bu dialogda uch oy davomida o'rgangan zamonlaringiz tabiiy ravishda birga ishlaydi.
grammarFocus: Aralash takror: Past Perfect, Present Perfect, Future — birga

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Ninety days! You've completed the whole course. How do you feel?
dialogue.uz: To'qson kun! Butun kursni tugatdingiz. O'zingizni qanday his qilyapsiz?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Proud and full of gratitude. Three months ago I had never spoken English with anyone.
dialogue.uz: Faxrlanaman va minnatdorman. Uch oy oldin hech kim bilan inglizcha gaplashmagandim.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: You have persevered even on difficult days. That's the real secret.
dialogue.uz: Hatto qiyin kunlarda ham sabot bilan davom etdingiz. Haqiqiy sir shu.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: Will I get a certificate?
dialogue.uz: Sertifikat olamanmi?

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Yes, but fluency is more important than any paper. What will you do next?
dialogue.uz: Ha, lekin ravonlik har qanday qog'ozdan muhimroq. Keyin nima qilasiz?

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: I'm going to continue every day. I'll watch films and read the news to get more exposure.
dialogue.uz: Har kuni davom etaman. Tilni ko'proq eshitish va ko'rish uchun film ko'raman, yangiliklar o'qiyman.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Great. If you can, immerse yourself — travel, make friends and use every resource you find.
dialogue.uz: Ajoyib. Iloji bo'lsa, tilga sho'ng'ing — sayohat qiling, do'st orttiring va topgan har bir manbadan foydalaning.

dialogue.speaker: Aziz
dialogue.en: So learning a language is a lifelong process.
dialogue.uz: Demak, til o'rganish — butun umrlik jarayon.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.en: Exactly. This is not the end — it's your first step beyond B2.
dialogue.uz: Aynan. Bu oxiri emas — B2 dan keyingi birinchi qadamingiz.
